articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Lower Millrace
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in May.
body: The group has raised $3,400 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Sunday mornings.
The Lower Millrace Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Felix Lombardi, who has lived in Lower Millrace for 6 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: St. Brendan’s Parish Announces New Hours for Spring
articles.deck: Residents of Eastgate filled the hall on Tuesday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The plan calls for senior exercise class along Quarry Court, with work expected to start in April.
Gloria Jablonski, who has lived in Eastgate for 29 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Public works estimates the work will take about 29 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Hickory Ridge Residents Push for Bike Repair Clinic
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 5 people and say bike repair clinic is the main draw.
body: The group has raised $48,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The effort began in October when a handful of neighbors met at the Hickory Ridge rec center to talk about bike repair clinic.

Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Hickory Ridge rec center on Tuesday at 7 p.m. The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

Several residents on Clover Avenue said they had been waiting since 1973 for something like this. Irene Murphy, who has lived on Clover Avenue for 5 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.deck: Friends remember Mariana Thibodeaux for the many years of service to Lower Millrace.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Lower Millrace.

articles.title: Council Tables Community Garden Ordinance
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Eastgate Avenue disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. Public works estimates the work will take about 6 weeks once it starts in March.

Residents of Eastgate said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.

Councilmember Janet Fontaine asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $1,200. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
